frequency_question: How often do major legislative packages containing explicit provisions for interstate energy infrastructure siting and permitting successfully pass both chambers and receive presidential signature?
membership_rule: Members are major omnibus or standalone energy/permitting reform packages explicitly aiming to reform interstate pipeline or infrastructure approvals; excluded are minor technical amendments, single-agency rule adjustments without statutory changes, or provisions entirely stripped before final passage.

cases.name: Energy Policy Modernization Act attempts (115th Congress)
ENERTIA Act / various permitting reform proposals (116th Congress)
Manchin Permitting Reform Bill negotiations (117th Congress)
Fiscal Responsibility Act permitting provisions (118th Congress)
Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (118th Congress)

coverage_note: 5 major distinct legislative vehicle attempts identified across 4 recent Congresses
known_gaps: Excludes minor rider amendments attached to must-pass appropriations bills that only marginally touched infrastructure without comprehensive permitting reform.
skeleton: named cases explicitly tracked across recent congressional sessions
validity_reason: Base rate tied to legislative polarization dynamics and committee structures which typically persist across two to three congressional cycles.
